title: [P0] Gallery sync push blocked by the required status check I added
description:
Making 'Validate gallery contract' a REQUIRED status check on master (2026-07-28 ~15:45) broke the release workflow's metadata.yaml push. bypass_pull_request_allowances lets the bot bypass the REVIEW requirement but NOT required status checks, and a direct push carries no check run for that commit:

  remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/master.
  remote: - Required status check "Validate gallery contract" is expected.

Timeline: v2.0.0 sync 12:20 SUCCESS (before the check was required) -> check made required ~15:45 -> v2.0.1 sync 15:50 FAILED.

IMPACT: the newest metadata.yaml entry is faeb174 (v2.0.0), which PREDATES the categories fix. The gallery is serving a template.tpl with no 'categories' entry - the gallery-compliance fix from gtm-5kv never actually reached the gallery. v2.1.0's sync will fail the same way.

REPAIR: a single v2.1.0 gallery entry covers everything (categories + Brands/Publishers switching), so no backfill of v2.0.1 is needed - but the push mechanism must be fixed first.

OPTIONS:
(a) Remove the required status check. One API call, restores automation, loses the merge gate.
(b) Migrate master to a GitHub ruleset with axeptio-bot as a bypass actor - rulesets support bypassing status checks; classic branch protection does not.
(c) Have the sync open a PR instead of pushing directly, with auto-merge. Keeps the gate AND validates the generated gallery entry before it lands, which a direct push never did. Needs allow_auto_merge enabled (currently false).

Repo currently has no rulesets; classic protection only.
close_reason: Sync mechanism fixed in PR #62 and proven by the v2.1.0 release: the workflow's 'Open the metadata.yaml sync PR' step succeeded, PR #63 opened with auto-merge enabled, and Validate gallery contract passed on it. The remaining one-click approval is tracked separately as gtm-3od.

title: [P0] Template delisted from GTM Gallery: LICENSE must be Apache 2.0 only
description:
SUP-1008: 'Our GTM template is no more in the GTM template gallery. It's a very big problem.' Reported 2026-07-28 11:34 UTC by samuel via Slack.

ROOT CAUSE: commit 9971689 (2026-07-27 11:18 UTC, PR #45 -> #48) replaced the Apache 2.0 LICENSE with Axeptio's proprietary licensing notice. Google's gallery requirement is absolute: 'the contents of the license file must be ONLY Apache 2.0' (developers.google.com/tag-platform/tag-manager/templates/gallery). The gallery monitoring system detects a non-conforming repo structure and automatically removes the template. ~22h elapsed between the merge and the report, consistent with the documented 2-3 day monitoring cadence.

FUNDAMENTAL CONFLICT: a template cannot both be listed in the GTM Community Template Gallery and ship under Axeptio's proprietary licensing terms. ENG-13012's objective is incompatible with gallery distribution for this repo. This needs a legal/business decision, not just a technical fix.

RECOVERY (per Google docs): restore the required structure (template.tpl, metadata.yaml, LICENSE containing only Apache 2.0 at repo root), then RESUBMIT via tagmanager.google.com/gallery -> Submit Template. Re-adding is not automatic.

NOT AFFECTED: axeptio/GTM_consent_mode_template still has Apache 2.0. axeptio/axeptio-sgtm-public-template made the same license change at its v1.2.0 (2026-07-22) but its metadata.yaml still carries placeholder homepage/documentation ('https://www.example.com'), so it was probably never submitted to the gallery - meaning it was NOT a valid precedent for this change, contrary to what was assumed when planning.

PROCESS FAILURE: the gallery licensing requirement was never checked before merging the license migration. Any future change to LICENSE, metadata.yaml, template.tpl location or the default branch must be validated against the gallery requirements first.
notes:
RESUBMISSION ATTEMPT FAILED (2026-07-28): 'The template already exists in the gallery'.

Interpretation: the gallery registration for this repo was NEVER deleted. What Google's docs call 'removed from the gallery' is a SUPPRRESSED/unpublished listing while the repo is non-conformant, not a deregistration. Consequences:

1. Resubmission is the WRONG action and will keep failing. The path back is passive: restore conformance (done) and wait for the next monitoring pass to re-validate and re-publish. Docs cite 2-3 days.
2. This neither confirms nor refutes the LICENSE root cause. It only tells us the registration survived.

FASTEST WAY TO THE AUTHORITATIVE ANSWER: the gallery emails the submitter about problems found during review ('make sure email notifications are enabled so that you can be notified of any issues that arise during template review'). Whoever originally submitted this template should check that inbox - it likely states exactly why the listing was pulled. That beats further inference.

CANDIDATE CAUSES, all landed in the same window 2026-07-27, all now restored except where noted:
  - LICENSE replaced with proprietary terms (restored, v2.0.0)
  - '# Latest version' markers stripped from metadata.yaml (restored, PR #54)
  - metadata.yaml header rewritten (restored)
  - default branch flipped develop -> master (still master; master holds all resources, which satisfies the docs)
  - develop branch DELETED (permanent - if the gallery had been reading resources from develop, that would explain the failure and cannot be undone by restoring files)
  - Issues disabled (has_issues=false) - PRE-EXISTING, not caused by this work, but a documented ongoing requirement and a live variable

NEXT: check the submitter's notification email; enable Issues to remove that variable; wait ~2-3 days; escalate to Google if still missing after ~5 days.
close_reason: Resolved by v2.0.0 (PR #56): LICENSE restored byte-identical to pure Apache 2.0. Listing confirmed live on the Community Template Gallery on 2026-08-05 — loaded the page directly. scripts/validate-gallery.py now enforces the Apache-only rule as a required status check, so the same regression cannot merge again.

title: Release automation broken: public repo cannot call internal tech-scripts reusable workflows
description:
Both release caller workflows in this repo reference reusable workflows in axeptio/tech-scripts, which is an INTERNAL repository. This repo is PUBLIC.

GitHub rule: a public caller repository can only access reusable workflows from PUBLIC repositories.
https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/reusable-workflows

Evidence:
- gh workflow run create-release-pr.yml --ref develop -> 'workflow was not found. See .../reusing-workflows#access-to-reusable-workflows'
- auto-release.yml run 30255471346 (triggered by the PR #39 merge) failed with ZERO jobs = access-time failure
- axeptio/tech-scripts visibility=INTERNAL, actions access_level=organization
- This repo: allowed_actions=all, so it is NOT an allow-list problem
- The reusable workflow exists and is valid at pinned SHA 88cc1b36b18292319f78e840160909ac195a9306 with 'on: workflow_call'

Consequence: PR #38 (develop) and PR #39 (master) could never have worked. master now has auto-release.yml that fails on every push, and release-please was deleted, so this repo currently has NO working release automation and zero tags/releases.

Fix options:
(a) Revert to release-please authenticated with BOT_GITHUB_TOKEN - exactly the pattern used by the sibling PUBLIC repo axeptio-sgtm-public-template, proven working through v1.3.0. release-please-action is a public action so there is no access restriction.
(b) Mirror the tech-scripts reusable workflows into a PUBLIC repo.
(c) Inline the ~16KB reusable workflow body into this repo (creates drift from canonical, must be maintained).
(d) Make axeptio/tech-scripts public - not viable, internal tooling.

Recommended: (a).

Related: ENG-11756 (canonical release automation spec) assumes internal/private callers and does not cover public repos - the deploy-release-automation skill should gain a visibility precondition check.
close_reason: Shipped as v1.0.0. Single-branch on master; release-please + commitlint aligned with sgtm; GTM Gallery sync automated (scripts/update-metadata-version.mjs); Apache 2.0 replaced with Axeptio licensing terms from 1.0.0.

title: Signing step never fires: gated on release-please's pr output instead of an existing PR
description:
The 'Sign the release PR commit' step added in a5375fe (PR #81) was gated on steps.release.outputs.pr != ''. That output is only set when release-please creates or updates a PR IN THAT RUN. Pushing a non-releasing ci/docs/chore commit leaves it empty, so the step is skipped and an already-unsigned release PR is never repaired.

Observed on run 31098131334 (master 592fa3c, the merge of #81 itself): release-please had nothing to update, outputs.pr was empty, 'Sign the release PR commit' = skipped, and PR #79's 61aba01 stayed unsigned. The fix shipped without unblocking the thing it was written to unblock.

Second miss on the same problem, same root cause both times: validating the happy path only. #80 fixed a guard never tested against a release PR; this fixed signing but was never tested against a run where release-please does nothing.

Fix: a 'Detect an unsigned release PR' step that asks GitHub whether an open release-please--* PR exists and whether all its commits are verified, and gates checkout, GPG import and signing on that. Also avoids force-pushing an already-signed branch on every push to master.
close_reason:
Fixed on fix/sign-any-open-release-pr. Gating moved from release-please's pr output to a 'Detect an unsigned release PR' step that queries GitHub directly.

Verified against the live repo BEFORE opening the PR, all three paths:
- unsigned release PR present (#79) -> emits branch=release-please--branches--master--components--axeptio-gtm-public-template, exit 0
- fully signed PR -> [.[].commit.verification.verified]|all returns true on #81, false on #79, so the skip is real
- no open release PR -> filter yields empty, no output, checkout and GPG import both skipped

Signing step replayed in a scratch worktree against #79's real branch with the push as --dry-run: one commit, subject 'chore(master): release 2.1.3' read from git rather than the PR title, signature G, 3 generated files, --force-with-lease matching the live tip feec717 (the branch had moved again since 8324437).

Lesson recorded: both this and gtm-1xr shipped after validating only the path I expected. The guard was never run against a release PR; the signing step was never run against a no-op release-please run.

title: Release PR unmergeable: release-please commits are unsigned and Compliance has no bypass
description:
PR #79 (release 2.1.3) could not be merged: 'Commits must have verified signatures'. 61aba01 'chore(master): release 2.1.3' is unsigned.

Root cause: release-please authenticates with a PAT (BOT_GITHUB_TOKEN) and the release commit it creates through the API is not signed. required_signatures sits on the Compliance ruleset with bypass_actors = [], and rulesets grant no implicit admin bypass — so nobody, including PLB, can merge it.

Not a regression in release-please: PR #69 (release 2.1.2, 2026-08-05) was equally unsigned and merged only because classic branch protection still gave admins an implicit bypass. The ruleset migration in gtm-3od removed that. The rule is working as written; this is the first release to meet it.

Rejected fix: adding axeptio-bot to Compliance's bypass. Bypass is per-RULESET, not per-rule, so it would also exempt the bot from required_status_checks and undo the gtm-3od guarantee that the sync PR cannot merge while the gallery contract check fails.

Chosen fix (PLB, 2026-08-06): a 'Sign the release PR commit' step in release.yml that rebuilds the release branch as one commit signed with BOT_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY — the key the workflow already imports for the metadata sync commit. No security control weakened.
close_reason:
Fixed on ci/exempt-release-please-from-merge-guard (PR #80): 'Sign the release PR commit' step in release.yml rebuilds the release branch as a single commit signed with the bot's GPG key, replaying VERSION / CHANGELOG.md / .release-please-manifest.json onto master.

Verified by extracting the step verbatim from the YAML and replaying it in a scratch worktree against the real #79 branch, with the push as --dry-run: produced one commit, exactly those 3 files, signature status G (good), and the --force-with-lease pin matched the live remote tip 8324437. Documented in docs/release-automation.md.

Side benefit: replaying onto master drops the 'Merge branch master into release-please--...' commits, so the Lint commits exemption from gtm-1xr becomes a backstop rather than load-bearing.

title: Merge guard blocks the release PR (release-please merges master into its own branch)
description:
Introduced by the gtm-vuv guard in PR #78 (d321b92). The step rejects any PR branch containing a merge of the base branch into itself. release-please's action keeps its release PR current by doing exactly that — commit 8d99e01 'Merge branch master into release-please--branches--master--...' — so 'Validate commit messages' went FAILURE on PR #79 (release 2.1.3). That check is required on master, so the release was blocked outright.

Missed when validating the guard: it was replayed against contributor PRs (#64, #73, #75, #76, #77) but not against a release PR, because none was open at the time.

Fix: exempt the release-please branch, scoped to author == axeptio-bot AND head_ref starting with 'release-please--' so a contributor cannot opt out by naming a branch to match. Safe because that branch holds only generated files, carries no contributor commits to prune, and its changelog is computed before the merge.

The gallery sync PR is unaffected: release.yml builds chore/sync-metadata-<tag> from a fresh master checkout with one commit and no merges.
close_reason: Fixed on branch ci/exempt-release-please-from-merge-guard: an 'if' on the guard step skipping it when the PR author is axeptio-bot AND the head ref starts with 'release-please--'. Documented in docs/release-automation.md, including why the gallery sync PR needs no exemption.

title: Migrate master to a ruleset so the bot can bypass status checks
description:
Classic branch protection cannot express 'this actor bypasses required status checks'. bypass_pull_request_allowances only covers the review requirement, which is why the release workflow's direct push to master was rejected with GH006 (gtm-wu9).

Worked around in PR #62 by having the gallery sync open a PR with auto-merge instead of pushing. That is better in one respect - the generated entry is validated before it lands - but it completes unattended only if the bot's bypass extends to merging its own PR without an approval. Unconfirmed; will be settled by the first release after #62.

If it does NOT complete unattended, migrate master from classic branch protection to a GitHub ruleset with axeptio-bot (or the bot team) as a bypass actor. Rulesets support bypass actors for ALL rules including required status checks.

Care required: classic protection and rulesets both apply if both exist, most restrictive wins. The migration must remove the classic required_status_checks entry at the same time, and must preserve: 1 required review, required signed commits, required conversation resolution, no force pushes, no deletions, and the bot bypass on reviews. Snapshot the protection JSON before changing anything - a full PUT replaces the whole object.
notes:
MIGRATION APPLIED 2026-08-05, awaiting empirical confirmation.

Classic protection removed (404 — no double-enforcement). Three rulesets on ~DEFAULT_BRANCH:
  Compliance  bypass=[]                  deletion, non_fast_forward, required_signatures, required_status_checks
  Review      bypass=[User:227449740]    pull_request (1 approval, thread resolution)
  Copilot     bypass=[]                  copilot_code_review

Required checks: Validate gallery contract, Validate commit messages, Validate PR title. Deliberately on Compliance, which has NO bypass — so the bot still cannot merge a sync PR that fails the gallery contract check. That preserves the validation benefit PR #62 introduced.

Bypass scoped to the axeptio-bot USER (227449740) rather than the BOT team, so it cannot widen if team membership changes.

Every item on this bead's preservation list verified present.

DELIBERATELY NOT CLOSED. This bead exists because a previous assumption about bypass semantics (that bypass_pull_request_allowances covered self-merge) proved wrong in production. Structural verification is not proof. Close only after the next release's sync PR merges unattended — if it stalls at REVIEW_REQUIRED again, the bypass mode or rule placement is wrong and needs another pass.

Residual nit: Review.allowed_merge_methods is ['merge','rebase'] while the repo has rebase=false. Inert; repo setting wins.

title: Support Brands/Publishers (TCF) selection in the GTM tag
description:
A customer needs TCF (Publishers) in some countries and non-TCF (Brands) in others. Axeptio geolocated display only selects among configurations WITHIN one product, so crossing Brands<->Publishers requires two projects and a client-side choice before SDK load.

Two blockers in template.tpl:
1. id validates against ^[0-9a-fA-F]{24}$ which rejects a {{Variable}} reference.
2. The SDK URL is hardcoded to the Brands build (https://static.axept.io/sdk.js) in BOTH the injectScript call and the inject_script permission allowlist. A Publishers Project ID alone would still load the Brands SDK, so no TCF banner could render.

Fix: new 'product' SELECT field with macrosInSelect:true (so it takes a GTM variable) defaulting to brands; select the SDK URL from it; allowlist https://static.axept.io/tcf/sdk.js; relax the id validator. Non-breaking - existing tags have product undefined which resolves to brands.

Customer: two Project IDs 6a22da4da7d365c1e246783d and 6a69dd80d632e1a5a9f03167.
notes:
BLOCKED: https://static.axept.io/tcf/sdk.js is an ES MODULE, not a classic script. Verified with V8: brands sdk.js parses as a classic script (control PASS), tcf/sdk.js fails with 'Unexpected token export'; the bundle ends with ;export{um as init,Ri as lookupConsentIndexFromCookiesVersionOrConfigurationId};. Earlier grep for top-level import/export returned 0 only because the bundle is minified onto few lines.

GTM injectScript creates a classic <script> and offers no attribute control, so the Publishers path in PR #60 cannot work. Worse, it fails silently: the file returns HTTP 200 so onload fires and the tag reports gtmOnSuccess while the SDK never initialises - green tag, no banner, no consent, on a TCF property.

Needs a product-side fix: a classic loader (e.g. static.axept.io/tcf/sdk-loader.js) that creates the type=module script itself. Template then points at the loader. PR #60 otherwise stands.
close_reason: Shipped in v2.1.0 (PR #60): 'Axeptio product' SELECT with macrosInSelect, per-product SDK URL selection, tcf/sdk.js added to the inject_script allowlist, and the Project ID validator relaxed to accept a GTM variable. Published to the gallery.

title: Sync released version into metadata.yaml so the GTM Gallery publishes it
description:
The GTM Community Template Gallery publishes template versions from metadata.yaml's 'versions:' list (each entry is a commit sha + changeNotes). Nothing in the release flow updates that file, so a cut release does not reach the gallery - metadata.yaml stays hand-maintained.

Reference implementation: axeptio/axeptio-sgtm-public-template runs scripts/update-metadata-version.mjs after release-please publishes, then commits metadata.yaml with the bot's GPG key:

  - name: Sync metadata.yaml version history
    if: steps.release.outputs.release_created == 'true'
    env:
      RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag_name }}
      RELEASE_SHA: ${{ steps.release.outputs.sha }}
    run: node scripts/update-metadata-version.mjs

Port that script and wire it into whatever release mechanism this repo ends up with (see gtm-22z). If the canonical thin-caller auto-release.yml is used, the sync needs its own workflow keyed on 'release: published' since the caller cannot add steps.

changeNotes text still needs a human-meaningful summary - decide whether to derive it from the CHANGELOG entry or keep it hand-written.
close_reason: Shipped as v1.0.0. Single-branch on master; release-please + commitlint aligned with sgtm; GTM Gallery sync automated (scripts/update-metadata-version.mjs); Apache 2.0 replaced with Axeptio licensing terms from 1.0.0.

title: Beads pre-commit export leaves issues.jsonl dirty after every commit
description:
core.hooksPath is .beads/hooks; its pre-commit runs 'bd hooks run pre-commit', which re-exports .beads/issues.jsonl but does not stage it. The export therefore lands in the working tree AFTER git has snapshotted the index, so every commit touching beads finishes with issues.jsonl modified again and needs a 'git add + commit --amend' to fold in. Hit three times in one session.

Beads has a supported option for this: export.git-add (default false). Setting it true in the tracked .beads/config.yaml makes the export stage itself, so the commit is complete and the tree stays clean. Fixes it for every clone, not just one.
notes:
VERIFIED on branch fix/beads-export-staging.

Before: 'git add .beads/ && git commit' -> hook exports issues.jsonl after the index snapshot -> commit excludes it -> 'git status' shows ' M .beads/issues.jsonl' -> needs 'git add + commit --amend'.

After (export.git-add: true): commit 5c0cef9 contains BOTH .beads/config.yaml and .beads/issues.jsonl, and 'git status --short' is clean apart from the untracked docs/superpowers/. No amend required.

Managed hook shims in .beads/hooks/ deliberately left untouched — they carry 'This section is managed by beads' markers and would be overwritten on upgrade. The config option survives upgrades.
close_reason: Shipped: gtm-ib3 via PR #71 (export.git-add: true in the tracked .beads/config.yaml); gtm-495 via PR #68 (logo header, four badges, repo topics).

title: Canary: alert if an Axeptio SDK URL stops loading as a classic script
description:
template.tpl injects two SDK URLs via GTM's injectScript, which creates a plain <script>. Sandboxed JS cannot set type="module", so both bundles MUST stay loadable as classic scripts:

  https://static.axept.io/sdk.js       (Brands)
  https://static.axept.io/tcf/sdk.js   (Publishers/TCF, IIFE per tcf-cmp-client#299)

If the TCF build ever reverts to esm, the failure is silent and severe: the file still returns 200, so onload fires, gtmOnSuccess is called, and the tag reports success while the SDK never initialises. Green tag, no banner, no consent collected - on a TCF property that is a compliance failure that looks fine.

CRITICAL - do NOT implement this with 'node --check'. Node >=20 detects module syntax, so 'node --check' PASSES on an ES module and the canary would be permanently blind to the exact regression it exists to catch. Confirmed on node v22.18.0: 'printf "const a=1;\nexport{a};" | node --check' passes.

Use vm.Script, which is what a classic <script> actually does:

  curl -s <url> -o /tmp/t.js && node -e "new (require('vm').Script)(require('fs').readFileSync('/tmp/t.js','utf8'))"

Proposal: a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (weekly) running that against both URLs, failing loudly if either stops parsing as a classic script.

Deliberately NOT added to scripts/validate-gallery.py: that is a required status check on master, and making it depend on an external CDN would let a blip block every unrelated PR.
close_reason:
Implemented in 2ee507e: scripts/check-classic-script.mjs + .github/workflows/sdk-canary.yml (weekly + workflow_dispatch).

Built exactly as the bead specified — vm.Script, never node --check. Re-confirmed the trap on this machine (node v22.18.0): 'printf "const a=1;\nexport{a};" | node --check' still exits 0, so node --check would have been permanently blind. The warning now lives in the script's header, not only in this bead.

Verified before shipping: the script rejects an ES module (data: URL, exit 1) and both live bundles pass today — static.axept.io/sdk.js 706351 bytes, static.axept.io/tcf/sdk.js 273742 bytes, exit 0. A canary that is red on day one is worse than none.

Kept off pull_request and out of validate-gallery.py, per the bead: that is a required status check and a CDN blip must not block unrelated PRs.

title: Early-consent block may replay the other project's consent
close_reason:
Fixed in 3043bc0. Two guards in the early-consent block, both failing safe.

Investigation result the bead asked for: there is NO project id in axeptio_cookies. widget-client/src/types/consent.ts:10-28 is the full payload — $$completed, $$googleConsentMode, $$cookiesVersion, $$token, $$date, $$duration, $$scope, vendor flags. The only discriminator is $$cookiesVersion.name (an object {name, identifier}, written by both SDKs), which is the value the tag already collects as data.cookiesVersion.

Second finding, which is what actually closes the reported scenario: $$googleConsentMode is written ONLY by the Brands SDK. tcf-cmp-client/src/google-consent-mode.ts:250-259 builds its cookie payload without it and calls gtag('consent','update') directly. So a Publishers tag finding that key is by construction looking at another project's data — guard 1 skips the cookie outright, which works even when Cookies Version is blank (the default).

Guard 2 covers Brands-to-Brands: skip when the tag's Cookies Version and the cookie's name are both set and differ. Deliberately lenient — a strict match would silently disable early consent for every tag leaving the optional field blank.

Residual gap tracked in gtm-ked: two Brands projects where either tag leaves Cookies Version blank remain indistinguishable.

5 scenarios added to ___TESTS___ (25 -> 30 passing). Each mutation-verified: removing guard 1 fails 'A Publishers tag never replays consent from the shared cookie'; removing guard 2 fails 'A cookie written by another configuration is ignored'; making guard 2 strict fails both lenient-path scenarios.

title: Add CI validation for the GTM Gallery submission contract
description:
Nothing in .github/workflows validates the Community Template Gallery contract (only commitlint.yml and release.yml exist). A violation is discovered only as a silently stalled listing 2-3 days after release — exactly the SUP-1008 failure mode. Google publishes no submission-status feedback, so CI is the only place this can be caught.

Live violation found while auditing: template.tpl has no `categories` entry in its ___INFO___ block (grep -c categories template.tpl -> 0), which the submission docs list as required (1-3 values). The LICENSE-must-be-Apache-2.0 rule was the other violation, fixed by PR #56.

Docs: https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/tag-manager/templates/gallery
acceptance_criteria:
New .github/workflows/validate-gallery.yml runs on PRs to master and asserts:
- metadata.yaml parses as YAML and has homepage + documentation + versions
- every versions[].sha exists and is an ancestor of master
- versions are newest-first, and the top entry keeps the "# Latest version" marker (SUP-1008 regression guard)
- exactly one template.tpl at repo root
- template.tpl ___INFO___ has a categories entry with 1-3 supported values
- LICENSE exists, all-caps filename, contains Apache 2.0 text
Workflow is required on master and fails red on each violation.
notes: PR #58 open, stacked on #57. Python + PyYAML confirmed acceptable by PLB. NOTE: the Validate gallery contract job has NOT run in CI yet - the workflow triggers on pull_request with branches:[master] and #58 currently targets fix/gtm-5kv-template-categories. It runs once #58 is retargeted to master after #57 merges. All checks were proved to fail locally first (categories removed, proprietary LICENSE restored, PLACEHOLDER_SHA, missing marker, swapped entries, non-ancestor commit, unresolvable sha). Issues-enabled is warn-only by design: sibling repo axeptio-gtm-public-variable has has_issues=false and stays listed.

title: Make the release changelog resilient to merge-commit pruning
description:
release-please generated the 1.1.0 changelog from only 2 of the 5 commits that PR #36 landed. All five were new since v1.0.0 and reachable from master, but the three authored on the fork branch in June were dropped - most likely pruned when the traversal crossed the 'Merge branch master into master' commit that pulled released v1.0.0 history into that branch.

Patched by hand in 735dad2 before cutting 1.1.0, because that changelog section becomes the GTM Gallery changeNotes via scripts/update-metadata-version.mjs, so an incomplete section ships an incomplete public description.

This will recur for any PR from a fork that merges master back into its own branch. Options: ask contributors to rebase rather than merge master in; or add a release-PR check that diffs the changelog bullets against 'git log <last-tag>..HEAD' and flags conventional commits that are missing. Verify the changelog on the next few release PRs before merging.
close_reason:
Prevented rather than detected, in 2ee507e.

Chose to remove the trigger condition instead of building a changelog-vs-git-log differ. A step in the existing 'commits' job of commitlint.yml fails any PR whose branch contains a merge of the base branch into itself: for each merge commit in base..head, if a parent is already an ancestor of the base sha, that merge pulled released history back in — which is what makes release-please's traversal prune.

Placed inside the 'commits' job deliberately: 'Validate commit messages' is already a required status check on master, so the guard is enforcing with no ruleset change.

Validated against real history before shipping — extracted the step verbatim from the YAML and ran it under bash: PR #73 fails on c2d4776 'Merge branch master into feat/gtm-seg-test-runner' (exit 1); PRs #64, #75, #76, #77 pass (exit 0). No false positives.

Merges of other branches are untouched; only a parent already on the base branch trips it. CONTRIBUTING.md documents the rebase workflow and why (9695134).

title: Verify v1.0.0 appears in the GTM Community Template Gallery

For an already-listed template, adding an entry to metadata.yaml's versions: list is the publish action; the gallery picks it up automatically, typically within 2-3 days of the commit.

Note: template.tpl at f731863 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the previously published version b0ccc441. v1.0.0 carries no template code change - it exists to put the gallery-distributed template under Axeptio's licensing terms. Same pattern as v1.2.0 in axeptio-sgtm-public-template.

title: Ask the SDK team to put the project id in axeptio_cookies
description:
The GTM template's early-consent guard (gtm-775) can only tell projects apart by $$cookiesVersion.name, because the cookie carries no project identifier. Confirmed against both SDKs: widget-client/src/types/consent.ts IUserChoices and tcf-cmp-client/src/google-consent-mode.ts axeptioCookiesProps. Neither writes clientId.

Residual gap that leaves open: two Brands projects on one domain where either GTM tag leaves Cookies Version blank (it is optional with no default) are indistinguishable, so the first project's Consent Mode state is still replayed for the second.

Adding $$clientId — or an identifier on $$cookiesVersion that the tag can be configured with — would make the guard exact rather than best-effort. Cross-repo: belongs to widget-client and tcf-cmp-client, not here. Raise with the SDK team / Linear before any template change.
notes:
Escalated to Linear: ENG-13297 (High, Engineering)
https://linear.app/axeptio/issue/ENG-13297/sdk-let-two-axeptio-projects-coexist-on-one-domain-identify-and
Driver is National (UAE, ENG-13144): one GTM container serving Brands OR Publishers geo-routed on one domain.

DECISION 2026-08-06 (PLB): shared consent across the two products is acceptable for National. They do not need independent consent per product on one domain.

Consequence for this bead: only the ATTRIBUTION half of ENG-13297 matters here — an optional project id in the cookie payload, which turns the template's heuristic into an exact check. The separate-cookie-names half is deferred in Linear; do not wait on it.

Why sharing is workable: TCF's authoritative record is the TC string in localStorage (tcf-cmp-client/src/poc.ts:540, sdk.ts:566), not axeptio_cookies — for TCF that cookie is a convenience mirror for the dataLayer. The two products collide in the mirror, not in the consent proof.

IMPORTANT — shared storage does NOT make cross-product replay acceptable. Guard 1 in PR #77 (Publishers tags never replay the cookie) must STAY. Deriving Consent Mode signals on a TCF property from consent never collected under TCF rules is a compliance question. If anyone cites this decision to argue for removing guard 1, that needs a legal/DPO view, not an engineering one.

SEPARATE REPO-SIDE FINDING, live today and independent of ENG-13297: the cookie NAME is already configurable in Brands (jsonCookieName / authorizedVendorsCookieName / allVendorsCookieName / gppCookieName — widget-client/src/sdk/SDKSettings.ts:94-97, default in constants/defaults.ts:10) but HARDCODED in TCF (tcf-cmp-client/src/google-consent-mode.ts:299-301). template.tpl reads getCookieValues('axeptio_cookies') with the name hardcoded and its get_cookies permission allowlists that exact string, so a Brands customer who already sets a custom jsonCookieName gets an early-consent read against the DEFAULT name — potentially another project's cookie. Making the template follow the setting needs a get_cookies permission change, which triggers a fresh gallery review (same constraint as ENG-13144 section 4).

title: metadata.yaml never got a v2.0.1 entry
description: The versions list jumps from v2.1.0 (eed87fd1) straight to v2.0.0 (faeb174c). v2.0.1's gallery sync failed silently (required-status-check blocked the bot push) and was never repaired, so the gallery's published history skips that version. Not a contract violation — the validator only checks that entries are real, ancestors and newest-first — and v2.1.0 supersedes it, so this is cosmetic history only.
close_reason:
Won't fix — backfilling the entry would be actively wrong.

v2.0.1 was the 'fix(ci):' release: CI-only, template.tpl unchanged. Adding it to metadata.yaml now would republish a superseded, contentless version to the gallery — precisely the noise PR #75 was built to stop, and the same defect as the 'Release v2.1.2' entry currently sitting at the top of the versions list.

v2.1.0 supersedes it, and validate-gallery.py is satisfied either way: entries need only be real commits, ancestors of master, and newest-first. There is no user-visible benefit to offering an old CI-only build as a selectable gallery version.

Recorded as a decision rather than left open as a task nobody will do.

title: Set the GitHub repo homepage and tidy its description
description: repos/axeptio/axeptio-gtm-public-template has an empty homepage field and the description 'Google tag manager template for the Axeptio cookies tag'. Both render above the README. Repo-settings change, not a code change.

title: Type CI-only changes as 'ci:' not 'fix(ci):'
description:
release-please's changelog-sections marks type 'ci' hidden, but 'fix(ci): ...' has type=fix and scope=ci — so it is VISIBLE in CHANGELOG.md and triggers a patch bump. Because scripts/update-metadata-version.mjs derives the GTM Gallery changeNotes from the top CHANGELOG section, a CI-only change then ships to gallery users as a public release note.

Happened in v2.0.1: 'fix(ci): make the validator run on Python 3.7+ instead of 3.10+' appears in the gallery notes for a change that does not touch template.tpl at all. Harmless once, noisy if it becomes a habit.

Rule: if a change does not affect template.tpl or metadata.yaml, type it 'ci:' or 'chore:' (both hidden, neither releasing). Reserve 'fix:'/'feat:' for changes a gallery user would care about.

Worth adding to CONTRIBUTING.md's commit-conventions section, where the type table currently explains version impact but not changelog/gallery visibility.
notes:
FULLY ADDRESSED as of PR #75, alongside #66.

Two halves of one problem:
  #66 — filters which CHANGELOG lines reach the gallery changeNotes (section allowlist).
  #75 — fixes which commits cut a release at all (docs/refactor/build made hidden, therefore non-releasing).

Root cause was that in release-please a VISIBLE changelog-sections entry is also a RELEASING one. That is not obvious from the setting name and cost two bad releases: v2.0.1 published a fix(ci) subject to the listing, and v2.1.2 was a docs-only release whose template.tpl was byte-identical to v2.1.1's, published with notes 'Release v2.1.2'.

Note the original framing of this bead — 'type CI-only changes as ci: not fix(ci):' — was a convention fix for a config problem. Scope never affected releasability; only type did. fix(ci) still releases and still publishes, so the convention remains worth following, but it is no longer the only line of defence.

Residual signal: a release whose changeNotes fall back to 'Release <tag>' now means something released that should not have. Documented in docs/release-automation.md.
close_reason:
Fully addressed across PR #66 and PR #75.

#66 filtered which CHANGELOG lines reach the gallery changeNotes (section allowlist: breaking changes, Features, Bug Fixes, Performance Improvements, Reverts).
#75 fixed which commits cut a release at all — docs/refactor/build are now hidden and therefore non-releasing.

Root cause was that in release-please a VISIBLE changelog-sections entry is also a RELEASING one, which is not evident from the setting name. It cost two bad releases: v2.0.1 published a fix(ci) subject to the public listing, and v2.1.2 was a docs-only release whose template.tpl was byte-identical to v2.1.1's, published with the notes 'Release v2.1.2'.

The bead's original framing — 'type CI-only changes as ci: not fix(ci):' — was a convention workaround for a config bug. Scope never affected releasability; only type did. fix(ci) still releases and still publishes, so the convention remains correct, but it is no longer the only line of defence.

title: Retire the Validate PR title job or enable squash-merge
description:
The Lint commits workflow runs amannn/action-semantic-pull-request to gate the PR title. It was ported from axeptio-sgtm-public-template, where PRs can be squash-merged so the title becomes the commit message. This repo has allow_squash_merge=false and allow_rebase_merge=false, so PRs land as merge commits and release-please parses the individual commits instead - the title never becomes a commit message.

The job is currently hygiene only. Either drop it, or enable squash-merge and make it load-bearing. Low priority, no impact either way; filed so the redundancy is a deliberate choice rather than drift.

Context: docs/release-automation.md and CONTRIBUTING.md already describe the merge-commit reality correctly (fixed in 546e0ad).
close_reason:
Resolved by rejecting its premise, not by acting on it.

The bead assumed the PR title 'never becomes a commit message' and so the Validate PR title job was hygiene-only. That is wrong. The repo is set to merge_commit_message: PR_TITLE, so GitHub writes the PR title into the merge commit BODY, and release-please parses it like any other commit. Evidence: merge commit 1e37fc6 for PR #64 has subject 'Merge pull request #64 from ...' and body 'docs: expand the README and correct the gallery description', and that body appears as its own entry in CHANGELOG.md.

So the title is load-bearing: a PR titled fix: cuts a patch release and publishes that line to the gallery, even when every commit inside it is chore/ci/docs. Retiring the check would have removed the only guard on a string that can trigger a public release.

Decision (PLB, 2026-08-06): keep the behaviour and keep the check required. The alternative — merge_commit_message: BLANK, which would make the title inert, remove the duplicate changelog entry, and let the check be retired — was considered and declined.

Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/release-automation.md so contributors know their PR title is a release artifact.
